title: Sequential function-vector executor over a shared recurrent block
hypothesis: For a learnable noncommutative operator family, applying a support-extracted function vector at each step of one shared transition block will execute held-out ordered operator pairs with high exact accuracy and preserve ordered intermediate states, while matching a same-width native learned operator-code control at <=90% of its actual serialized inference bytes.
physical_object: One shared state transition block recurrently applied twice.
mirror_coordinate: A support-extracted 16-dimensional function vector for each operator, addressed in the order requested by the two-step program and supplied to the same recurrent block at each step.
logical_multiplicity: Eight logical operators and held-out ordered two-operator programs executed by one physical transition block.

task.type: synthetic affine bijections over four-bit states
task.worlds: Eight random invertible GF(2) affine maps x -> A x XOR b per world, with operator maps and pair programs generated from world seed.
task.training_examples: All 8*16 atomic mappings and all 12 non-held-out ordered operator pairs on all 16 input states.
task.evaluation: All 16 start states for each of four held-out ordered pairs; additionally audit all atomic maps and intermediate-state correctness.
task.support_query_boundary: The per-operator support pair sets are extraction inputs. Held-out composition targets are never used for code extraction, training or model selection.

methods: support-extracted FV with one tied recurrent transition block (candidate)
same-width directly learned native operator-code bank with one tied recurrent block (strong simple control)
support-extracted FV with a one-shot two-operator decoder and no explicit state passing
native operator codes with untied depth-specific transition blocks (independent-depth upper control)
external two-call execution of the candidate's shared transition block, feeding the predicted first intermediate into the second call
exact stored operator lookup tables (quality upper; complete tables charged)

development.training_loss: Endpoint cross entropy for atomic and ordered pair examples; no oracle intermediate-state labels or recurrent data augmentation.
development.sampling: Paired deterministic minibatch stream; equal atomic and pair example probability, fixed by world seed and update index.
development.selection_metric: No tuning or selection; one fixed configuration.

fresh.access_condition: Open only if both development worlds have FV held-out pair exact accuracy >=90%, intermediate-valid path rate >=90%, FV accuracy no more than 5 percentage points below the native-code tied control, and actual FV inference payload <=0.90x that control.

secondary: internal unroll vs external two-call latency

storage.authority: Actual uncompressed deterministic NPZ inference payload bytes plus canonical configuration, with all state needed by each method included.
paid_objects: operator-code extractor and support examples for FV at inference
native operator code bank for the control
exact operator tables for upper control
all method metadata and code ordering

compute.runtime: Measure batch-1 internal two-step unroll and external two-call execution separately; exclude compilation and warm up consistently.

success_gate: On every fresh world, FV held-out ordered-pair exact accuracy >=90%, intermediate-valid path >=90%, within 5 percentage points of native-code tied control, and serialized FV payload <=0.90x native-code control. Report external two-call results separately; no capacity claim from operator count.
failure_gate: Either development world misses a quality threshold or FV payload exceeds 0.90x native-code tied control; fresh remains sealed.
boundaries: Synthetic algebraic function family only; no natural-language result.
Support extraction and the code retrieval address are charged; support/query composition targets remain disjoint.
A sequential unroll is not parallel token generation and may add inference compute.
A direct lookup table is an upper reference, not a learned-FV result.
A pass would establish only this bounded synthetic execution mechanism, not independent capacity.
